# Agents

## Understanding Agents 

What is an AI agent? There are a lot of definitions of agents floating around the internet and debating the semantics of these definitions is a bit of a trap. 

To understand typical agents in the context of AI it is helpful to understand the problem they solve. Let's look at a conversation with ChatGPT asking for a single line birthday wish to a friend.   
   
![][image5]

Notice the LLM does not output a single sentence initially. We need to prompt it again in order to get the desired output. 

What if instead of having a human prompt the LLM until we accomplish a **task** we had software do this?

Recursively prompting a LLM until a base case (**task**) is met is a **Goal Oriented Agent** and it helps us achieve better outcomes without human intervention. The agent makes a decision to either call the LLM again or stop and return the result. 

![][image6]

## Building A Basic Agent

Now it's time to build a basic single agent system. 

1. Click on create new workflow and name it OneAgent

   ![][image7]

2. Create a new agent and use the Generate with AI feature to fill out the details with the prompt.  “Create an agent that generates a birthday wish.” Click Apply Suggestions.

![][image8]

3. Select the llama model for the agent to use and click create agent. Alternatively you can just copy the fields as below instead of using the AI suggestions.   
   ![][image9]

Three important Crew AI specific ideas here:

**Role:** Describes what the Agent is responsible for.  
**Backstory:** Gives a brief history that explains where the Agent came from and what it’s experienced.  
**Goal**: States what the Agent is trying to achieve or prioritize during the mission.

Now that we have an agent in the workflow we need to assign it a task.

4. Close the create agent window and click Save and Next to go to the Add Tasks. Create a task with the same details as the one below. Note the name of your agent might be different because it was generated by AI\!   
     
   **Task Description:** Create a birthday message that is only one sentence. Make sure that it is only one sentence. Double check this before returning the output.   
   **Expected Output:** One sentence birthday message.

    

   ![][image10]

   

5. Once you fill out the task description and the expected output **make sure to click add task.** The Flow diagram will update to show the Task assigned to the agent you created in the last step.   
     
   ![][image11]  
6. Click save and next to progress to the Configure stage. (At this point the workflow gets saved as a draft automatically.)  Leave the default token and temperature settings and click save and next to get to the Test stage. Click run Workflow to test your Agent\!

![][image12]

A few interesting things to note. You have the ability to playback the events that happened using the Playback slider. This is very useful in understanding how the agent executed. We can get a lot more detail from the logs and monitoring tab. For this lab we're not going to look at monitoring in depth, but lets take a look at some of the details you get with Agent Studio Monitoring.  
![][image13]

This JSON is generated by Crew AI. Look at the property max\_iter=10. Remember we said earlier an agent gets to decide how many times it calls an LLM? Here we have a limit of 10 calls before we must return the answer. 

Now take a look at how Crew AI used the info about our agent and our task to prompt the LLM.
